statement: Consider a unit-free canonical ordinary CNF state with n=9,m=12,L=36, hence all live variables have incidence degree exactly 4. Eliminate a selected degree-4 pivot with polarity split 2+2. Let U be the total number of nonpivot literals in the four pivot clauses and R the literal count of the eight retained clauses. Then R+U+4=36, R>=16, so U<=16. The four raw resolvents have total literal count at most 2U. Therefore the post-elimination literal count is at most L'<=R+2U=32+U<=48. Consequently if all eight remaining variables stay live, the next minimum incidence is at most floor(48/8)=6; if fewer stay live, the variable-count frontier only improves.
proof: Unit-free means each of the eight retained clauses has width at least two, so R>=16.
The four pivot clauses contain exactly four pivot literals plus U tail literals, and R+(U+4)=L=36; hence U=32-R<=16.
With split 2+2, each positive tail participates in two resolvents and each negative tail in two resolvents. Before tautology removal/dedup/subsumption, the sum of resolvent widths is at most 2U.
Thus raw retained-plus-resolvent literal mass is at most R+2U=(36-4-U)+2U=32+U<=48. Canonicalization cannot increase it.
If n'=8, averaging gives d'_min<=floor(L'/8)<=6. If n'<8, fewer future eliminations remain; this lemma is used only as a sufficient reachable-state bridge, not as a general totality theorem.
